Al-Biqa'i, *Nazm al-Durar*, commentary on Surah al-Jinn (72), verse 7:

Since the sense is: the misguidance of each of the two groups in regard to the other is a far-reaching error, to the point that they have strayed far from the prophetic laws and have held beliefs that it is not permissible to hold, namely denial of the Creator (*ta'til*) and belief in nature (*i'tiqad al-tabi'a*), so that the matter remains thus: wombs expel and the earth swallows, with no messenger to guide them and no resurrection of the dead to their Creator. Their saying is conjoined to this, emphasizing it in the recitation with *kasra* (the reading *inna*, with a kasra on the hamza), to point to the manifestation of the proofs of resurrection, and that it is hardly to be believed that anyone would deny it. This alerts us that caprices and errors may be agreed upon by a vast multitude, as an exhortation to the one who is guided not to feel lonely on the path of guidance because of the scarcity of those who travel it, and not to be deceived by the paths of perdition because of the multitude of those who perish. ﴿And that they﴾, i.e. the humans, if they were addressing the jinn, and the jinn, if they were addressing the humans, ﴿thought﴾, i.e. the jinn or the humans, a thought about which they were not certain (*ʿala thalj*, lit. "on snow," i.e. not firmly settled). Opinion may hit the mark and may err, and erring is more common. ﴿as you thought﴾, i.e. O jinn or humans. The meaning in the reading with *fath* (the reading *anna*, with a fatha on the hamza) is: "It has been revealed to me that the humans or the jinn thought," and the clause ﴿that﴾ fills the place of the two objects of *zanna* (to think). ﴿that﴾, i.e. that the great matter ﴿would never﴾ (*lan*, emphatic, to show the intensity of their denial of it) ﴿raise﴾ (*yab'atha*). They indicated the error of this thought by using the divine name, saying: ﴿Allah﴾, i.e. He who has complete encompassing knowledge and power, ﴿anyone﴾ (*ahadan*), i.e. after his death, because Iblis confused them, so that they saw as good what was not good; or [it means] any one of the messengers who would remove by him the blindness of ignorance, and what the humans were subject to by the jinn's leading them astray, and other misguidance besides that. It has become evident from the Qur'an that this thought is false, and that resurrection is necessary in both matters, for it is the wisdom of the King and the special concern of the King.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 72, verse 8:

Since the denial of resurrection stems from a defect in power, they proceeded to affirm the completeness of power in a manner that indicates the soundness of the Qur'an and its protection from the jinn, lest one suppose that it is of the same kind as the soothsayers' (kuhhan) utterances. So they said, emphasizing it in the recitation with kasra (inna) to express the remoteness of reaching the heaven, as an exhortation to seek great matters even if their place is far away: ﴿And that we﴾. Since seeking thoroughly (al-imān fi al-tafttīsh) is expressed by "iltimās" (groping/searching), and stripping the verb (tajrīd al-fi'l) is greater than that in indicating lightness and absence of hardship, he said: ﴿we touched the heaven﴾, i.e., the lower heaven (al-dunyā), we sought its news as was our custom for listening to what a person is led astray by, a seeking that is like sensing by touch with the hand. ﴿Then we found it﴾ from all its sides, and it is from wijdān (finding). ﴿Filled﴾, i.e., a filling that is in the utmost ease and lightness for its doer. ﴿With guards﴾, i.e., guards, a collective noun, so it is singular in form, and for this reason it was described by his saying: ﴿severe﴾, i.e., by the angels. ﴿And meteors﴾, plural of shihāb, which is what blazes from fire. Their aspirations were elevated until they sought worldly matters and carnal desires from a journey of five hundred years upward. So woe to him who is lazy about the established matters of religion from a journey of an hour or less, and who does not sit in a gathering of knowledge for an hour or less. The expression "al-mala'" (the filled/guard) indicates that they were guarding before that [-], but not in [-] this manner. It was said: they guarded at the descent of the Torah, then the guarding intensified for the Gospel, then it was filled at the descent of the Qur'an, so they were prevented from listening at all, except for what the Qur'an confirms, as a prelude (irhāṣ) to the great final prophethood, lest some kind of confusion occur through them.

When they had reported about its state at that time, because that was the most important matter for them, they were told about its state earlier. They said, emphasizing against what the humans held, namely the denial that anyone could reach the heaven: ﴿And we used to sit in it﴾, that is, in the past, ﴿in positions﴾ from the heaven, that is, many positions, which we knew, with no guard over them, so they were suitable ﴿for listening﴾, that is, because we would listen from it to some of what the angels speak of, concerning what they were commanded to arrange. It has come in a report that the manner of their sitting was that one of them would be above the other until they reached the heaven. Abu Hayyan said: whenever the uppermost was burned, the one beneath him would take his place. They would snatch a word and throw it to the soothsayers, and they would add lies to it.

Since the implied sense was: "so that we might listen from it to what is decreed for us without any obstacle," He followed it with His saying: ﴿So whoever now listens﴾, that is, strives to reach the hearing, ﴿now﴾, that is, at this time, regarding what is future. They divided time into what had been the case, the unrestricted permission of listening for them, and what the situation became of guarding. They applied "now" to the second entirely, because they meant only the time of their saying, or they meant it because they know what comes after it and so they allow that the state therein may be otherwise. ﴿will find for himself﴾, that is, for his sake, ﴿a flame﴾, that is, a blazing fire of shining, burning brightness.

Since the flame carries the sense of a plurality, because what is meant is that every place in it is like that, He described it with a singular noun of collective form, saying: ﴿a watcher﴾, that is, which those who hurl it keep watch over without any negligence. It is permissible that it be a verbal noun in intensive form, like "a just man." The *rasd* (watching) is vigilant expectation, because when there is no delay in hurling it as one approaches the heaven, it is as if it itself were the one watching for him, observing his affair, the attentive one who has no slackening and no negligence in any way. Rather, it is the watching itself, and this is its meaning in essence. Whenever he ascends to listen, it is hurled at him, which prevents him from listening, and if it overtakes him, it burns him. As for hearing, it has been ruled out by His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed they are removed from hearing﴾ [al-Shu'ara' 26:212].

When they were informed of their faith, that it occurred immediately upon hearing (the Qur'an) without any hesitation, they then mentioned their being prevented from eavesdropping. They mentioned that the prevention was confusing to them, so they did not know its secret. This shows that ignorance of some [subsidiary (*furu'i*)] matters is not detrimental, (p-479) and it is an exhortation to lift one's aspiration from delving into something without knowledge, and an urging to entrust the matter to the Knower of the unseen. Then they clarified what had driven them to traverse the easts and wests of the earth until they found the Prophet ﷺ reciting the Qur'an. They said, emphasizing (this) because the Arabs used to attribute to them knowledge of the unseen and the solving of difficult problems: ﴿And we do not know﴾, meaning, in any respect, even if we resist and strive (to know), ﴿whether evil is intended﴾. Since what was feared was the very act of willing in the past [not its being from something known, even though the agent is known, namely the chooser who possesses the decisive past will], they constructed the verb in the passive, saying ﴿is intended﴾, teaching good manners in that evil is shunned from being attributed to Him, glorified is He, since there is no difficulty in knowing that nothing occurs except by Him. ﴿for those on the earth﴾, meaning, by this guarding, from which misguidance arises. ﴿Or has their Lord intended for them﴾, meaning the One who is good to them and manages their affairs. They constructed it in the active voice regarding the good, informing and teaching good manners that His mercy precedes His wrath, and indicating that He may have intended by this prevention good, ﴿guidance﴾, meaning rectitude, from which good arises. Thus the verse is an instance of *ihtibak* (a rhetorical device of mutual implication): mention of evil first as an indication of good second, and guidance second as an indication of wealth first.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 72, verse 11:

When He, glory be to Him, informed [of the ease of their faith], it might have been thought that this was only because their disposition was inclined to submission, so He followed it with what shows that this extraordinary matter (ﷺ) was [a sign] for his sake, and that it came into being for his glorification and honour. So He said, relating their words, emphasizing (because the preceding speech clearly indicates the soundness of the nature of them all): ﴿And among us﴾, that is, O jinn, ﴿are the righteous﴾, that is, those who are deeply rooted in the quality of righteousness, which prepares one to accept every good.

Since the one who is not righteous may be corrupt, either by actually engaging in corruption and intending it, or by not directly engaging in it, they said, attentive to the ranks of knowledge and of deeds that bring nearness or distance: ﴿And among us﴾, and they put the adverbial phrase first because it is attached to a indeclinable word, so it is said: ﴿beneath﴾, that is, a people in a lower rank ﴿than that﴾, that is, this noble, lofty quality.

Since what is beneath the righteous has many kinds according to its readiness for corruption or righteousness, its preparedness for it, or its distance from it, they fittingly explained this by saying: ﴿We are﴾, or a state which is like a natural disposition, ﴿sects﴾, that is, possessors of paths, which are doctrines and many aspects. They used "paths" to refer to their adherents, indicating how intensely they are clothed in them.

Since separation may be by the least thing, he showed that it is in the highest degree, so he applied to them the very word for what is cut off and described them with it, saying: ﴿sects﴾, that is, (ﷺ) groups divided, whose inclinations are scattered, the plural of "qidda", which is a group of people whose inclination is other than theirs, from "qadd", which is a cutting that causes a great division, like the thongs cut from hide, cut so that each group is separate by itself. Al-Hasan and al-Suddi said: disbelievers and Muslims, Rafidah, Mu'tazilah, Murji'ah, and other than these, like the sects of mankind.

When they showed their subjugation in what they had been able to do regarding [the matter of] the heaven, by what they mentioned, and [showed] the subjugation of their corrupters through this Qur'an from much of what they used to do to the people of the earth, they were in truth subdued by this Qur'an, which is of great standing, from the two horizons [east and west]. So We prevented them from it and protected it through it. And they indicated that they were the locus of subjugation through dispersal. That was a cause for knowledge of the all-encompassing power of the Exalted, so that no seeker can reach Him and no fugitive can escape from Him, because of the aspects of His greatness and dominance that He displayed to them in guarding and otherwise. Then He, glorified is He, mentioned the effect of that upon them, namely their acknowledgment and submission to the One, the Subduer. He said, relating about them that, as an exhortation to follow their example in knowing the self through might and humiliation, and weakness through dispersal and division, and in knowing the Lord, glorified is He, through complete power, sovereignty and greatness, through the complete singularity that does not admit likeness or division:

﴿And that we﴾ They emphasized it, against the assumption of humans about their strength, which is not what it is. ﴿Thought﴾ They used "thought" for "knowledge," indicating that the intelligent person ought to avoid whatever he imagines to be harmful, even by the least kinds of stratagems, so how much more when he is certain [...] (p-482) ﴿that﴾, i.e., that the matter is great. They added further emphasis to what preceded, saying: ﴿we shall never escape God﴾, i.e., that we could resist Him if He intended harm to us, because of His encompassing of everything in knowledge and power, for He is One, without any like. They indicated the aspect of [weakness –] by their saying: ﴿on earth﴾, i.e., dwelling in it and remaining in it, and it is the direction of the lowest, which entails subjugation, and that is the utmost of our effort. So where are we from the vastness of His dominion, which is in His grip? ﴿And we shall never escape Him﴾, i.e., in any way whatsoever, ﴿by flight﴾, i.e., as those who flee, or from the direction of flight, i.e., we fled from the earth to something else, for the heaven prevented us, and there is no place for us to move except in His grip. So where, or to where, is the refuge? By that they denied both avenues of deliverance: meeting [Him] and victory, and flight when subdued.

(p-483) When the one who suspects may or may not act on what his suspicion requires, they made clear that what they meant by it was knowledge, and that they hastened to act upon what it called them to. So they said, emphasizing against the jinn's reluctance and difficulty: ﴿And that when we heard the guidance﴾, i.e., from the Prophet (ﷺ), ﴿the guidance﴾, i.e., the Qur'an, which has such complete nobility (ʿarāqa) in the quality of eloquent exposition and in calling to good that it is fitting for the very name "guidance" to be applied to it, ﴿we believed in it﴾, i.e., without any hesitation at all, acting upon what it has of this great quality.

Since the implied sense is: "So we believed, by reason of our belief, which was led to us by the guarding of the heaven from being struck by it (the meteors), given His complete power over us, which guided us, and which prevented us from listening through the guard," they traced their statement to that, acknowledging their inability to resist the threat from the King, and seeking refuge in His protection and holding fast to His rope: ﴿So whoever believes﴾, i.e., brings into being the reality of faith and continues to renew it at every moment.

When they understood that His calling them to Him and His explanation of the way, together with His complete power, came only from the generality of His kindness and mercy, they mentioned the quality of beneficence to increase the encouragement, and said: ﴿in his Lord﴾, i.e., the One who is good to him, among us and others.

Since the believer is the one singled out from among all creatures for salvation, he introduced the particle fa (then) into the response and made it nominative, under the assumption of a subject (mubtada'), to indicate this, and to indicate that their salvation is a necessary matter. So he said: ﴿then he will not﴾, i.e., he in particular [not] ﴿fear﴾ at all ﴿deficiency﴾, i.e., decrease, scarcity, wrongdoing, and harshness in reward and honor in any way whatsoever, ﴿nor oppression﴾, i.e., something disagreeable that overtakes him and overpowers him, because he has done nothing of that sort to anyone so that he would be repaid for it. This is an exhortation to the believer to avoid such things, lest he be repaid with them. The context indicates the supposition: "And whoever associates anything with Him, then he will not feel secure from injustice nor from being overtaken."

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 72, verse 14:

When this was apparent in that they all accepted Islam, they said, negating this apparent meaning and emphasizing that their Islam, [along with] their intense aversion, is hardly believable: ﴿And among us are the Muslims﴾, meaning, O jinn, ﴿the Muslims﴾, meaning those who are sincere in the attribute of Islam to the Guide, so they surrendered to Him their leadership. Thus they are upright in that, equitable, and steadfast; they do not part from the guide, so they are on the straight, just, and pleasing path. ﴿And among us are the deviators, the disbelievers﴾, meaning those who swerve from the most upright course and fall into the wastelands and trackless deserts where there is no signpost; thus they are disbelievers in their Lord. ﴿And among us are the equitable.﴾ "Qasata" means he acted unjustly with injustice, dropping him from the rank of humanity to the rank of the lowest of animals; and "aqsata" means he removed injustice and so acted justly. So the verse is of ihtibak (a rhetorical device in which one term implies its opposite): "the Muslims" indicates the disbelievers, and "the deviators" indicates "the equitable."

Since they had known from what they heard of the Qur'an that resurrection for recompense is necessary, they made this division the cause of their statement: ﴿Whoever has submitted﴾, meaning whoever establishes Islam entirely, by submitting outwardly and inwardly to the guidance from the jinn and [from -] others. Since this was a context of encouraging the truth, He connected their act to its cause, and He praised them by saying: ﴿those have sought out﴾, meaning those of high rank, ﴿a right course﴾, meaning a great correctness and rectitude, having been, because of the deficiencies they had, straying from them; so they treated their souls until they possessed it and made it a dwelling for themselves. From their saying: "al-hara" (with the short vowel): the hollow of the sandgrouse where the gazelle shelters; and the region and the place. "Ma ahara-hu bi-kadha" means what made it obligatory for him; and "bi-l-hara an yakuna kadha" means he is deserving of being so; and "fulan hariyyun bi-kadha" means he is deserving. It may also come as "al-hurr" (without the ya'), meaning with effort. "Tahharaytu al-shay'" means I aimed at its direction. Thus that course became for them a means to Paradise. And from qasata, ﴿those﴾ [failed to strive, so they attained -] error and deviation.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 72, verse 15:

When they recognized that safety lies in holding fast to obedience to Allah, they alerted (the listeners) to the danger of exposing oneself to His seizure, and they said: ﴿And as for the deviators﴾ — that is, those who are deeply immersed in the attribute of tyranny, turning away from what is right, among the jinn and others. Those people neglected their own souls, so they did not seek what would benefit them, and they went astray, so they were distanced from the path, and they fell into the ruins from which there is no escape. ﴿They shall be⁠ — by their very natures — ﴾ ﴿fuel for Hell﴾, that is, the Fire of far-reaching depth, which will meet them with scowling, disapproval and frowning (p-486), ﴿fuel﴾ with which the Fire is kindled. So it is kindled as long as they are alive, and they are alive as long as it is kindled: they do not die and thus find rest, nor do they live and thus revive. Thus the verse is an instance of *ihtibak* (a rhetorical device of mutual omission), and it is an explicit statement, not an implication, required by the context: he mentioned seeking out (benefit) first, as an indication of its abandonment second, and he mentioned Hell second, as an indication of the omission of Paradise first. The secret of this is that they were in a station of warning, so they mentioned what is to be feared and omitted what must be known, because Allah, exalted is He, does not waste anyone's reward; rather He does not limit Himself to what corresponds to a good deed by custom, but He must add to it nine times its equivalent, and with Him is abundance. There is no power and no strength for us except through Him, glory be to Him and exalted is He.

When God, glory be to Him, made the jinn desire and fear through their tongues, by what He guided them to and what He illuminated their hearts with, and the preceding verse was the last thing He related about them, the implied meaning was: "It has been revealed to me that the deviators among my people and others, if they had believed, God would have done for them the good He did for the believing jinn when they believed. God would have enriched them in this world, by what is lawful, away from what is unlawful, without hardship. He would have clothed every bone they found with its fullest meat, and restored for them every dung they saw to its best state, by the blessing of this noble Prophet, upon whom be the best of prayers and the most complete of peace."

﴿And that﴾, that is, "And it has been revealed to me that the great matter" (p-487) ﴿if they had walked straight﴾, that is, sought from all creation, the jinn and humankind, the people, and brought it into being, remaining ﴿upon the way﴾ [that is] which has no other way, and which the jinn understood from the Qur'an as Islam and justice (iqsat), leading to success in both abodes.

Since water is the origin of every good, as God, exalted is He, said in the story of Noah, upon him be prayer and peace: ﴿He will send the sky upon you in abundant rain﴾ [Nuh: 11], and from it comes every living thing, and it was precious among the Arabs, He said, magnifying it by turning to the place of majesty: ﴿We would have given them to drink﴾, that is, We would have made for them, by what We possess of greatness, ﴿abundant water﴾, that is, much, great, of great benefit, by which We would multiply provision, adorn the land, and make life abundant.

[p. 488] Since His blessings are a bounty from Him, not something owed to Him for worship or anything else, God the Exalted said, informing us that their ultimate purpose is that one deserves reward or punishment for what He has prescribed for Himself, glory be to Him, and that "the Word is not changed with Him" (Qur'an 50:29). Also, everything He, glory be to Him and exalted, deals with His servants, of benefit or harm, is only a trial (fitnah) for them, drawing out what they have been created with of good or bad. ﴿That We may test them therein﴾, meaning: We deal with them in the manner of one who tests, by the greatness We possess, ﴿therein﴾, meaning: in that water from which the various kinds of blessings come, so that the state of the grateful and of the disbeliever may be revealed. Al-Razi said: "This is after He withheld the rain from them for years." He ended. Others said: 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "Wherever there is water, there is wealth, and wherever there is wealth, there is trial." Al-Hasan and others said: "They were hearing and obedient, then the treasures of Kisra and Qaysar were opened to them, and they were tested by them, so they rose against their Imam and killed him," meaning 'Uthman, may Allah be pleased with him. It is also permissible that the word be used figuratively for knowledge and the various kinds of cognitions that arise from acts of worship, which are for the souls as the souls are for the bodies. In this case, "trial" (fitnah) carries the meaning of purification (takhlis) from the worries and vices in this world and from the retributions in the Hereafter, as in "I purified (fattantu) the gold" when I cleansed it of its impurity.

Since the implied sense is: "Whoever turns to the remembrance of his Lord, We will bless him in the Abode of Peace forever," He followed it with His words: ﴿And whoever turns away﴾, meaning: a persistent turning away until death, ﴿from the remembrance of his Lord﴾, meaning: transgressing beyond the worship of the One who is good to him, who nurtures him, and from whom no other benefactor comes. ﴿We will make him enter﴾ [al-Hijr: 12], meaning: We will cause him to enter ﴿a punishment﴾ which will be like a thread passing through the hole of a bead, in extreme narrowness, [p. 489] ﴿severe﴾, meaning: arduous and intense, overpowering him, dominating him, and climbing over him. It will be, each day, higher than what came before it, as a fitting recompense, for turning away grows stronger the longer its duration is.

When the implied sense was: "Because He revealed to me that the matter is as you commonly accept among yourselves, that whoever serves other than his master, He will punish him forever," He followed it with another statement, explaining the way of the prophets, peace be upon them, and the perfection that is due to them, which comes through the two powers of knowledge and action, and the completion that comes through both together with the power of expression. Whoever is not perfect cannot be imagined to produce completion, just as there cannot be a true son of the loins from one who has not reached maturity, so there cannot be a true son of the heart from one who is not perfect. It also explains what is permissible for them, what is impossible for them, and the care that God Most High has for their affairs:

﴿And that﴾, i.e., and it has been revealed to me that ﴿the places of prostration﴾, i.e., the places of prostration in the macrocosm of the horizons, which is the earth, and in the microcosm of the self, which is the body, as Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Talq ibn Habib said, ﴿are for God﴾, i.e., exclusively belong to the Supreme King, ﴿so do not call upon﴾, i.e., because of that, O created beings, in the customary manner, ﴿along with God﴾, [i.e.,] the One who possesses all greatness, ﴿anyone﴾. For whoever worships other than his master in the dominion of his master, which is the macrocosm of the horizons, and with the instrument of his master, which is the microcosm of the self, is the most deserving of blame and punishment among people. So how fitting is it for you that He creates for you a face, and a hand, and two feet, and an earth from which you benefit, and a sky whose benefits are complete, and then you prostrate with the limbs He brought into being for you, on the earth in which He enabled you to benefit, under the sky whose benefits He has perfected, to other than Him? Thus you would have diverted to another the favor of the Master, the thanks for which is due to Him for it. Would any sensible person do this?

Al-Baghawi said: If ﴿al-masajid﴾ is taken to mean the places of prayer, then its singular is with a kasra on the jim (masjid). If you take them to mean the limbs, then its singular is with a fatha on the jim (masjad).

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 72, verse 19:

Since one who calls upon his master and devotes himself to him, performing what is obligatory upon him and fitting for those like him, is not rebuked for it nor is it considered strange, one is only surprised at someone who calls upon other than his master, or inclines toward him even slightly, so that one asks about the cause of it. [Allah] said, expressing astonishment at the iniquitous ones among the jinn and mankind: ﴿And that﴾, i.e., it was revealed to me, or the jinn said to those among their people who obeyed them, relating what they had seen of his ﷺ prayer and the crowding of his companions around him, marveling at that: that the matter, or the great and wondrous story, ﴿when﴾ I stood up, they almost became ﴾upon me﴿ — this is how the original would have been, but He expressed it with "the servant" as was previously stated, that one who calls upon his master, even if that master were the most insignificant of existents, would not be treated in that way by him; so how much more so when his master is the Owner of the kingdom and the King of kings — ﴿the servant of Allah stood up﴾, i.e., the servant of the Supreme King, to whom all majesty and all beauty belong, so there is no existent that comes near Him; rather every existent is from the overflow of His bounty — ﴿calling upon Him﴾, i.e., (p-491) calling upon his master with the worship of a servant, from the standpoint of his being His servant, and from the standpoint of his master hearing whoever calls upon Him and answering him.

Since the iniquitous ones were most of the people — rather all the people in that era, jinn and mankind — [Allah] said, explaining that it is permissible for the prophets to be harmed and belittled, in order to raise their ranks and to console their heirs, even though their station refuses that:

﴿They almost became﴾, i.e., the iniquitous ones of both groups, the jinn and mankind, came close to being ﴿upon Him﴾, i.e., upon the servant of Allah, ﴿a heap﴾, i.e., piled up on one another from the intensity of their crowding, until that became their nature, marveling at what they saw of his worship and wishing to turn him away from it. This is a matter that should not be marveled at; rather what is marvelous is what they themselves did of worshipping others than Him, glory be to Him and exalted, and their marveling at the worship of His servant toward Him and his sincerity in calling upon Him. It is the plural of ﴿libad﴾ — with a kasra on the lam — and it was also read with a damma on the lam, the plural of ﴿lubdah﴾ with a damma, which is what has been matted, some of it upon other parts.

(p-٤٩٢) When, according to the reading with *kasr* (the *qirāʾah* of *kasr*, a canonical variant reading of the verse), the listener's soul became eager for his ﷺ words concerning those who massed against him, He resumed the answer with His words, clarifying what is impossible for the Prophets, upon them be prayers and peace, namely calling upon other than Allah, and leaving off calling upon Him, or opposing any part of His command. He said: Or, when his ﷺ soul yearned, according to the reading with *fatḥ* (the *qirāʾah* of *fatḥ*), for that which would repel what he saw from them, the Exalted said, guiding him to that: ﴿Say﴾, that is, to those who crowded upon you, counting them among the ignorant for what you do, because they acted as the ignorant act: ﴿Indeed I call upon﴾, that is, with the call of worship, ﴿my Lord﴾, that is, the One who brought me into existence and nurtured me, and I have no blessing except from Him alone. I do not call upon anyone else, so that you may marvel at me and then crowd upon me. The apparent meaning that comes first to understanding is that the meaning is: And it was revealed to me [that] when I stood [in prayer] worshipping Allah in the hollow of a palm tree, and the jinn whom Iblis had directed toward Tihamah [and] who heard the Qur'an saw me and crowded upon me until they nearly overwhelmed me, and some of them were upon others, and they heard my declaration of Allah's oneness, my glorification of Him, and His being singled out with power, knowledge and all the attributes of perfection, and they believed. It was also said: it is the report of the jinn to their people about the prayer of the Prophet ﷺ, and what his companions did behind him in their alignment in prayer, their surrounding him, and his admonition and teaching them. This view is attributed to Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with both of them, and Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, for that is a strange situation. It is related that the king of the Persians sent someone who had entered Islam when they (the Muslims) approached his lands, and among what was reported to him about them was that he said: When they pray, they arrange themselves in rows, and a man leads them. They stand with his standing, prostrate with his prostration, sit with his sitting, and do as he does, with no disagreement among them. When the king heard that, it alarmed him, and he said: What do I have to do with these people? What do I have to do with ʿUmar? Abū Ḥayyān related from Makḥūl that the number of those who followed the Prophet ﷺ on the night of the jinn reached seventy thousand, and they finished at the breaking of dawn.

Since the one calling upon his benefactor could possibly have associated another with him in his call, even with the slightest forms of association, and the restriction (in "I call upon my Lord alone") is understood according to what is most common, he deserved rebuke and crowding. He negated that with His words, emphasizing the meaning of restriction and confirming it: ﴿And I do not associate with Him﴾, that is, now or in the future, in any way whatsoever, ﴿anyone﴾, such as Wadd, Suwāʿ, Yaghūth and others, from among the inanimate and the animate.

When the listener may say, "Why does he not destroy them, or ask his Lord to repel those who oppress him by destruction or by repentance and following him?", He commanded him with what shows the greatness of his Lord, and that He does nothing except what He wills. With His words, showing that it is impossible for him, upon him be prayers and peace, to do what is impossible for all possible things, namely to have an effect on anything by himself or to oppose his Lord: ﴿Say﴾, that is, to these who opposed you. He emphasized it (p-494) to cut off the one who might believe, because of the many miracles he witnesses, that whatever he wills, God will do for him: ﴿Indeed, I do not control﴾, that is, now or later, ﴿for you﴾ by myself, without God empowering me, because there is no effective agent in anything except God, glorified and exalted.

Since the context is to repel their evil from him, He said: ﴿harm﴾, so it is understood "nor benefit, nor misguidance" ﴿nor right guidance﴾, that is, correctness and rectitude. The verse is of the type called ihtibak (a rhetorical device in which one term is mentioned and its counterpart omitted, and vice versa), and it is evident on this reading. Abu Hayyan said: "He omitted from each side what its opposite indicates" — end of quote. It is also possible that its meaning is: "I do not control harm, because I do not control misguidance for you, and I do not control right guidance for you, so I do not control benefit for you, for there is no benefit except in right guidance, and no harm except in misguidance." May God disgrace Ibn 'Arabi al-Ta'i, who says in his Fusus: "Misguidance is more guiding than guidance." There is no one of weaker intellect than him except those who follow him—may the curse of God and His disgrace be upon them. If they say: "He meant other than what the apparent wording conveys," then say: "You have lied, for his intended meaning has been made clear by your unanimous agreement on wickedness and immorality. Scarcely will you find among you anyone accused of his doctrine while he is bound by the Shari'ah." The verse does not leave the ihtibak by this, for mentioning "harm" first indicates the omission of "benefit" second, and mentioning "right guidance" second indicates the omission of "misguidance" first.

(p-495) When he had answered those who were eager to learn the reason for his patience in not repelling them from him, with an answer whose gist is this: he has nothing in his hand, because his God, in His greatness, encompasses knowledge and power, and nothing escapes His will. He does not hasten in anything, such that He only does what He wills, whether He is asked or not. This might have led one to suppose that he, ﷺ, would agree with them so that they would not harm him, since they hasten to harm whoever opposes them. He answered, with an answer whose gist is that he is between two harms: one from them if he opposes them, and the other from Him, glory be to Him, if he turns away from Him. He, glory be to Him, repels their harm if He wills, and they have no power to repel His harm in any way. So He said: ﴿Say﴾, that is, to the one who calls you to agree with them. He emphasized it because of what many people think, that causes do not fail, so He said: ﴿Indeed I﴾, and He increased the emphasis because that is most firmly fixed in souls, so He said: ﴿will never be protected﴾, that is, shielded from Him by one who protects a neighbour from his neighbour, ﴿from God﴾, that is, the One to whom belongs all command, and no one shares any command with Him, ﴿anyone﴾, that is, whoever he may be, if He, glory be to Him, wills evil upon me.

Since one with this standing might cause the seeker to flee from him, He said, emphasizing: ﴿nor will I find﴾, that is, at all. Since every rank is below his rank, and the ranks below his rank are very many because of his absolute exaltedness (p-496) and the levels of lowliness for others, which cannot be limited, He said, pointing to this with the preposition: ﴿other than Him﴾, that is, God, Exalted is He, ﴿a refuge﴾, that is, a place of escape, a place of inclination and reliance, an entrance, a shelter, and a means, even if you strive with all your effort. For ''laḥd'' (inclination) is originally deviation, and it is said only of a deviation from truth to falsehood. And ''ḥadd'': he disputed, contended, and inclined (rakana).

Since it is known that this is a matter with no ambiguity (mathnawiyya, literally "duality") in it, and since the ranks below His exalted rank, may He be glorified, are very numerous because of His absolute loftiness, and whatever follows them has the judgment of their nobility and reality, the first of these is the conveyance from Him, glorified be He, without an intermediary [then the conveyance through an intermediary] by His noble angels from Him. He made an exception from "refuge" (multaḥadan) by way of [no] "shelter and no escape from You except to You, so flee to Allah" [then he said]: ﴿Except a message from Allah﴾, meaning, one who conveys me, being ﴿from Allah﴾, that is, the One who encompasses everything in power and knowledge. But, out of the vastness of His mercy, He conducts affairs in accordance with what people know of them: that He does not seize anyone except with a proof that they acknowledge to be a proof. When he had explained the first rank, which is the highest, he followed it with the one that comes after it, and said: ﴿and His messages﴾, which were revealed to me [through] the intermediary of the Angel, for I receive them in the proper manner by preserving them and acting upon them, and that is what protects from every evil in this world and the next.

(p-497) Since the intended meaning is to show that Allah honored the messengers by giving them a portion of His greatness, so that disobedience to them is disobedience to Him, the recompense for one who disobeys them is the recompense for one who disobeys Him, glorified and exalted be He, because they speak only by His command. Thus, ﴿whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger, for him are gardens of bliss, wherein they will abide forever in happiness﴾. Then He joined to this His saying: ﴿And whoever disobeys Allah﴾, that is, the One to whom all greatness belongs, ﴿and His Messenger﴾, the one with whom He sealed prophethood and messengership, making his message encompass all of His creation in monotheism or otherwise, by way of denial, ﴿then indeed for him﴾, that is, specifically, ﴿is the Fire of Hell﴾, which meets him with scowling and rage. When He expressed it in the singular, looking to the wording of "whoever" (man), because it is more explicit regarding each individual, He expressed it in the plural, carrying it to its meaning, because it is more indicative of the generality of humiliation, and said: ﴿abiding therein﴾, and He emphasized the meaning and affirmed it against the claim of one who asserts that it ends, and so He said: ﴿forever﴾. As for one who claims that it burns but that its punishment is sweet, there is no one more insane than him, except one who follows him in his misguidance, error and falsehood. They have no repelling except the sword in this world and punishment in the Hereafter, for what they called sweetness, while they are destined to it and held in account before it.

(p-498) When he mentioned their massing against him, and placed first what is more important of his affair, which is removing their grief by informing them that what they denied him is what is due to him, and [that], along with his weakness in contending with them, he is [further from] turning away from God, since God is stronger than everything, and that he cannot but comply with His command, and he pointed out that they are powerless [against] His (glorified is He) assaults by their inability to give protection against Him, he stated this, threatening them. So he said, making their massing against him the limit: ﴿Until, when they see﴾, that is, with their eyes in it, ﴿what﴾, that is, the thing which. And since the dreadful part of the threat lies in its applying to everyone for whom the threat is meant, and not in its being from a specific person, he said: ﴿they are promised﴾, that is, whatever the threat was realized, whether in this world or in the Hereafter. As for the Hereafter, it is obvious. As for this world, it is like the expulsion of the Prophet (ﷺ) when the polytheists gathered to plot against him to kill him and strove toward that, and then his sariyyas (raids led by others under his command) and his ghazawat (military campaigns he personally led), such as the Battle of Badr and others, from the Days of God, which filled the earth with light and the people of truth with joy and delight, and the people of falsehood with loss, ruin, terror, destruction and graves. ﴿So they will know﴾, that is, from that day on which its interpretation occurs, through a promise with no breaking of it and no lengthening of its term, ﴿who is weaker in helper﴾, that is, in terms of the helper: I, even though at this time I am solitary and weak, or they, ﴿and fewer in number﴾, even though they are now such that none can count them but God (glorified is He). How great, by God, is the speech of the messengers, in that they consider themselves weak in themselves, and mention their strength through their Lord, in whose hand is the dominion and to whom belong the hosts of the heavens and the earth. This is in contrast to the people of atheism, for they have no speech except in magnifying themselves and belittling whoever is other than them; and if you dispute with one of their followers, he says, "This is on the tongue of prophethood," and the like of this is among their deceptions.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 72, verse 25:

Since it is well known that when they hear this threat, they say, out of mockery, blindness to the path of rectitude, and arrogance: "When will it happen? Let him hasten it," He resumed His speech as a reply to them, a reply from one who is not hurried or distressed by it, because he does not fear escape and is not harmed by the enemy's survival or their striving to harm his allies, clarifying what is permissible for the Messengers, namely that what is hidden from other humans may be hidden from them, while Allah informs them of what is hidden from others. ﴿Say﴾, i.e., in reply to them, if they deny and, mocking, ask about the time of the punishment's occurrence coming upon them: as for its occurrence, it is necessary, because the threat has been issued by One who does not break His promise; as for specifying its time, He, glorified is He, has concealed it, because that is more effective in intimidation. This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿I do not know﴾, i.e., I do not know in any way, even if I seek it out and take means toward it. He increased the affirmation of its concealment, and that it still lies within the category of what is asked about, by the form of interrogation, so He said, placing first what conceals it from them: ﴿Is what you are promised near?﴾, i.e., will it occur now or close to this time, such that it is expected imminently, ﴿or does my Lord appoint for it a long term?﴾, i.e., for this promise. Since the delay might suggest negligence toward the Friend, He said, dispelling that: ﴿My Lord﴾, i.e., the One who is good to me, whether He hastens it or delays it, ﴿a term﴾, i.e., a great appointed limit in every respect, such that even in distance it is not possible with that that it should occur now, nor that it be expected short of that term. So it is in every state awaited; therefore be on utmost guard, for it must occur. Its occurrence is not in question; what is in question is the specifying of its time.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 72, verse 26:

When he (ﷺ) had negated knowledge of the unseen from his own noble self, he negated it from others in a general manner covering all of the unseen, [and] there came from the greatness of the One who sent him what necks cannot bear. So He said, describing Him: ﴿The Knower of the unseen﴾, meaning all of it, which is what has not emerged into the world of witnessing. Thus He, glorified is He, is exclusive in its knowledge. [Therefore -] He made the consequence of this His saying: ﴿So He does not reveal﴾, meaning in any way at any time, ﴿His unseen to anyone﴾, [meaning -] that which He has kept hidden from others, so it is exclusively His, ﴿anyone﴾, because knowledge of the unseen is precious, and because it is exclusively the attribute of the King.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 72, verse 27:

Since He does not make the Unseen (al-ghayb) known except by manifesting it to the world of witnessing (ʿālam al-shahāda), and since the first one to whom it is disclosed has a nobility that ought to be recognized for him, He said: ﴿Except for whomever He has chosen (irtaḍā)﴾, meaning: whoever Allah, in His creating, has approved of, the action of one who deliberately seeks this and strives in it. He clarified "min" (from) by His saying: ﴿of a messenger﴾, meaning from among the angels and from among mankind, for He manifests to him that Unseen, to that chosen one who is described (p-501) — not to every chosen one — by revealing to him whatever He wills of it. This is because the Unseen is a genus (jins) that has no realization except within its individual instances; so when one individual of it becomes manifest, the genus has become manifest in it, through the manifestation of a portion of it.

Sometimes that messenger is an angel, and sometimes he is a human being whom Allah addresses without an intermediary, like Moses, upon him be peace, during the days of intimate conversation (munājāt), and Muhammad ﷺ on the night of the Ascension (miʿrāj) in the Higher World, in the presence of "two bow-lengths or nearer." When the messenger manifests it to him, it goes out of its being unseen, and the messenger conveys it to whomever He has permitted him to convey it to: sometimes by revelation (waḥy) for the prophets, and sometimes by inspiration (nafth) and direct inspiration (ilhām) for the saints (awliyāʾ). This occurs when their souls are prepared, their faculties being quieted from contending with the intellect through appetites and personal desires, just as it happens for souls in general at the time when the faculties are quiet from contention through sleep, so they become prepared for the inspiration (nafth) placed into them. Whoever turns away from the side of the senses and turns toward the side of holiness (qudus) has prepared his soul for the angel's inspiration into his heart, so that he knows what he did not know. There is no one among people who does not know from his own self that when he turns wholly toward something, there occur to him intuitive, inspired matters suddenly, without any prior thought or seeking. According to the degree of preparation, the inspiration comes from Allah, glorified and exalted. Sometimes the inspiration is satanic, by what the devils receive through eavesdropping from the angels, either from (p-502) the earth after their descent or from the heaven by stealing a hearing within it — and Allah knows best. It is also possible that the saints have direct speech (mushāfaha) from the angel, as Maryam, upon her be peace, had from the angels. Jibril, upon him be peace, said concerning some of them that if one of them greeted him, he would return the greeting.

Since this context indicates the rarity of knowledge of the Unseen, and its rarity is a reason for guarding the one to whom it is disclosed so that he conveys it to the one who commanded it, as it was commanded, Allah, glorified and exalted, informed of that by His saying, emphatically, to distinguish it from the knowledge of soothsayers, whose origin is from the jinn, and indicating the honoring, exalting, glorifying and ennobling of the messengers: ﴿Indeed, He﴾, that is, Allah, glorified and exalted, causes that messenger to know whatever of the Unseen He wills.

That is: when He wills to manifest it to him, ﴿He sends (yasluku)﴾, that is, He makes it enter in the manner of threading a string through a pearl, into his being and passage, without any slightest deviation toward other than the intended target. Since the purpose is achieved through those whom He places from His hosts for guarding, even if they are one from every direction, and indeed by other than that, and since He made this sending out for the command according to what the servants know of it, He expressed it with the preposition (al-jarr) as an indication that the watch does not encompass all directions to the farthest edge of the earth, for example, so He said: ﴿from before him﴾, toward the direction that the messenger knows, ﴿and from behind him﴾, that is, the direction that is hidden from his knowledge. Thus that becomes sufficient as a covering of every direction. It is possible (p-503) that mention of the two directions indicates the whole, and He singled them out because the enemy, whenever one of these two is left unguarded, comes from it, and whenever both are guarded he does not come from elsewhere; for it becomes between the first and the last ﴿a watch (raṣadan)﴾, that is, a guard from His hosts who protect him and keep him by preserving what is with him of the Unseen from being snatched by the devils or others, lest they steal anything of his news. This was said by Ibn ʿAbbas, may Allah be pleased with them both. Muqatil and others, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: they inform him about whoever denies it, by warning him against him if he is a devil, or commanding him to listen to him if he is an angel. That is because Iblis used to come to the prophets in the form of Jibril, upon him be peace, but Allah protected them from him.

The passage is an excerpt that begins mid-argument, so I have translated it as it stands.

When this pattern of protection was established for every messenger, al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) ended it with a comprehensive statement, specifying what the genus (al-jins) requires and clarifying that the singular form is intended in the plural sense, and that it was expressed only so that the protection would encompass each individual among them. So He said: ﴿That He may know﴾, meaning God knows with a knowledge that exists and occurs in this attribute, which His knowledge had already encompassed in eternity before its existence, with what none knows but Him, glory be to Him, that it will be, ﴿that﴾, meaning that the messengers, peace be upon them, ﴿have conveyed﴾, meaning to those to whom they were sent (p. 504) ﴿the messages of their Lord﴾, meaning the One who brought them into being, arranged all their affairs, and chose them for His messages in the state they are in, without any blemish touching them or any dust reaching them. Since this might give the impression that He needs watchers for the protection, He removed that by saying: ﴿And He has encompassed﴾, meaning that He does this while He has encompassed ﴿what is with them﴾, meaning the messengers and those to whom they were sent, from among the angels and humans, in the most precise, greatest and most wondrous ways, which is indicated by the expression "ladā" (with Him/with them). Since this was sufficient for the purpose, but limited to the place of need, He generalized the matter by defining it as it truly is. So He said, inducing the utmost certainty regarding what the messengers relayed from their Lord, and that there is no ambiguity in it nor any danger in any way, clarifying the ultimate clarity: He refuted the story of the "cranes" (al-gharaniq), which some exegetes and others mentioned in the sura "An-Najm": ﴿And He has enumerated﴾, meaning God, glory be to Him and exalted, ﴿everything﴾, meaning in general without any exception at all, ﴿in number﴾, meaning in terms of number, for everything that can be counted, even at the smallest measures of an atom, in what has passed and in what will continue. This is a decisive proof of His knowledge of particulars just as of universals. The beginning and end of the sura, its hidden unseen part and its outward part, have met. Its ending points to the general beginning, and its beginning points to the detailed ending. That is because the beginning of the sura explained the greatness of the revelation through the occasion of the jinn; then in its course it explained His protecting it from those who eavesdrop; and it concluded by emphasizing the protection of it and of all its words, and it continued to affirm His command until the greatness of this Qur'an became evident, and the might of this Criterion (al-Furqan) appeared above every book, in every respect and reckoning. So he opened "Al-Muzzammil" with something similar and ended it with the command to recite what is easy of it. In "Al-Muddaththir" he mentioned the slander of the slanderer against it, and what he incurred because of that slander of disgrace and punishment in this world and the Hereafter, along with the guarantee of its protection from him. Then in the sura "Al-Qiyamah" he forbade His Prophet (ﷺ) from haste in his matter, lest its protection be disturbed, or lest its wording deviate even slightly, [and] as legislation for his community in abandoning haste, for it is not the practice of men of resolve. Then he affirmed the matter of its revelation in "Al-Insan", and clarified that the cause of turning away from it is love of the fleeting life, which is itself the essence of deficiency. He ended "Al-Mursalat" with the furthest extent of what imagination, fancy and conjecture can conceive, so He said: ﴿Then in what statement after this will they believe?﴾ Glory be to Him who arranged this order, and made it the furthest of the intended aims and the ultimate of the desired goal, and may God bless forever the one after whom there is no prophet.
